advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add discrimination mutations that force the `is_placeholder` and anti-fork clauses of `assert_mint_registered` to go RED (e.g. mint a non-placeholder identity, and mint under a `jira-datacenter` provider), so all three oracle clauses are shown to have discriminating power, not just `minted is not None`.
evidence: assert_mint_registered asserts three independent clauses: `assert minted is not None` (_dc_support.py:261), `assert rebar.is_placeholder(minted, ...)` (_dc_support.py:267), and `assert forked is None` (_dc_support.py:273)

The only RED mutation, `test_the_oracle_goes_red_when_the_mint_is_a_no_op`, neuters the mint to a no-op and asserts the failure message contains 'THE PASS MINTED NOTHING' (test file:181,189) — this exercises the first clause only; the store is empty so execution stops at `minted is not None`

`test_the_oracle_goes_green_on_the_real_dc_mint` and the setup test only assert these clauses in the passing direction; no test drives a non-placeholder mint or a jira-datacenter fork to show `is_placeholder`/anti-fork can fire

ABSENCE rationale: a production regression narrowing to placeholder-vs-real identity, or forking the provider namespace, has a concrete failure path the module docstring calls out ('adopted or overwrote a real person's identity'; 'forking the identity namespace') yet no mutation confirms the oracle would go red on it
advisory.finding: The discrimination suite proves only the `minted is not None` clause of `assert_mint_registered` can go RED; the `is_placeholder(minted)` and anti-fork (`resolve_mapping('jira-datacenter', ...) is None`) clauses are only ever asserted in a green state, so a regression that made the mint create a non-placeholder identity, or fork under a `jira-datacenter` provider, would not be caught by any discrimination test even though the suite's explicit purpose is to prove the oracle HAS discriminating power.
